RESULT [labelnoise]: Detected real label errors in common test datasets with precision up to 71.5%, and 97% on a proprietary dataset, beating three baselines.
US [labelnoise]: This is a cheap, model-internal signal that can be logged per box during each incremental training round. Boxes whose loss stays high across epochs are candidates for rollback or review. It is complementary to ObjectLab.
CORRECTION [labelnoise]: WACV 2024 (pp. 4582-4591) is confirmed, as are precision up to 71.5% on real test datasets and 97% on proprietary data. The arXiv abstract lists three baselines; the WACV version's description mentions four, including a probability margin method.
RESULT [attribution]: Outperforms several baselines on the simulated benchmark. On real data it finds label errors with precision up to 71.5% on standard datasets and 97% on proprietary data, with low false-positive rates.
US [attribution]: This is an alternative or complement to ObjectLab for screening harvested batches, and it is simple to implement from YOLO's per-box loss terms. It is the concrete method for the 'analyse whether the new data caused the drop' step at box level once a batch fails the gate.
CORRECTION [attribution]: None needed. It outperforms all three baselines and is the only method that detects all four simulated error types efficiently. Real label errors are found with precision up to 71.5% (common test datasets) and 97% (proprietary), with low false-positive rates.
